Columnizer #1
A Note from the Column Government

Dear Schitz,

We as a team are actively improving our local communities by supplying affordable housing to consumers. Our ministries are taking active precautions to make sure that we are addressing the issues seen in Relayer as optimally as possible. Our goal is to benefit all people from all walks of life, race, and gender to ensure a welcome environment for families and businesses alike. The statistics that we use to carefully calculate what and where we build are only from the most trusted Scholar researchers, data analysts, and economists, so we can be proud to say that our developments are eco-friendly.

Thanks, Jannet Smith
Columnizer #2
A Complaint from a Ponderosa Citizen

I'm tired of these tramps coming onto these paths and blocking them when I go for my morning walks. One of them even tried to assault my son, who is only 7, and no one does anything around here! We need more funding for police around here to wipe out all of the vermin. The government is too damn liberal about these things! Like how they don't increase my pay and increase the taxes instead because of these damn homeless people.

Columnizer #5
A Page From a Book by Reywas Nesnah

Picture this, if you will. This place used to be a warm, flourishing place with birds and other animals that would be commonly seen wandering around here everyday. But now, after endless toxic rain, the infrastructure was destroyed, and all businesses lost their jobs. The Faucet Reef spilled out so much oil after the implosion, when the Oil River started to flow, that the people here went in droves to seek the medicinal plants below. Now, as a 15 year old, despite my age I see that this was not a freak accident like most people say. People here are so gullible that they will take everything at face value.
Columnizer #6
An Observation from Scholar Peitharchia Andras

You're gonna pay for this shit. It's impossible to publish anything. You will strike down any potential for publishing. You dictate every word I write. I know why: it's because you don't want me to go “off the rails”, and make us look bad, and maybe say that we did something wrong. 2 years of my life just for it to fly under the radar, just because of you? That last little bit? I've spent so long testing, experimenting, and getting to be in a lab like this one, let alone even becoming a Scholar in the first place. Stop making excuses. Stop being a narcissist. Have some fucking mercy. I'm going to find something new, and I'm taking my research with me.\n- Peitharchia
Columnizer #7
A Note from Pugna of the Volare Guild

Rest. Rest at the base. The great curved pillars of time and life, that stand forever absolute. I realize that this is the gateway to the abyss, but I never thought it could be so beautiful. The step below hell awaits on the true ground.\n\nThe Scholars come here in droves once a year, every year, to look at the progress of the lift. Every year it's just the same. A test subject goes down the lift, either dies, disappears, or comes back up never the same when they descended.
The Tale of Symfora
By Vetus the Prophet

Earth
And
Columns
That is all
We can live off of
We were born so close to the edge
Of insanity
Destined to
Control
All
Life

A note:
It seems like everyone here, on this column, is bound to go to the Scholars, and then attempt to try to revolutionize the world but then fall to some nihilism when they sell out. And if you don't become a scholar and were born below Ponderosa, you have no way to climb the ladder. The only true way to be contempt with life, I feel, is to fall back into nature; to go back to the roots. That does not mean to live in faith of God, or Azaprota, as it will push you to anger and destruction, like so many others who will fight and die over land and god.

When the pendulums of your life align from the polyrhythm within, for a moment, in that time and in that moment, you will be inside and outside this experience.
Close to the Edge
A poem from the tome "Bound Calamity" by Maynard Jack Kaiser
